{{Short description|Curve of a specific cubic implicit function}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''trident curve''' (also '''trident of Newton''' or '''parabola of Descartes''') is any member of the family of [[curve]]s that have the [[formula]]:

:<math>xy+ax^3+bx^2+cx=d</math>.

[[Image:Newton_trident.svg|thumb|300px|Trident curve with <math>a=b=c=d=1</math>.]]

Trident curves are [[cubic plane curve]]s with an ordinary double point in the [[real projective plane]] at <math>x=0</math>, <math>y=1</math>, <math>z=0</math>. If we substitute <math>x=x/z</math> and <math>y=1/z</math> into the equation of the trident curve, we get

:<math>ax^3+bx^2z+cxz^2+xz = dz^3,</math>

[[Image:Newton trident y=inf.svg|thumb|300px|Trident curve at <math>y=\infty</math> with <math>a=b=c=d=1</math>. This curve partially resembles the [[folium of Descartes]].]]

which has an ordinary double point at the origin. Trident curves are therefore [[algebraic curve|rational plane algebraic curves]] of [[geometric genus|genus]] zero.

Solving for <math>y</math>, we get

:<math>y=\frac{d}{x}-ax^2-bx-c</math>.

Solving for <math>x</math>, we get

:<math>x=\frac{d-ax^3-bx^2-cx}{y}</math>.
